title: FP8 attention kernel tuning for H100/H200 (tile + launch config) + microbench validation
author: Grace Kim
body:
Summary: Tune FP8 attention decode/prefill kernels for Hopper (H100/H200) by adjusting tile sizes and launch configuration to reduce shared-memory pressure and improve occupancy at common hosted shapes. Includes a small microbenchmark suite and reference numbers collected in perf-lab.

Motivation / context: During the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we saw H100/H200 underperforming FP16 at mid-seq decode for some common batch/concurrency mixes. Profiling pointed to lower-than-expected occupancy and smem-limited launches in the FP8 attention kernel variants (particularly at head_dim=128 with grouped-query attention). This PR applies Hopper-specific tuning and gates it behind runtime capability detection.

Key changes (H100/H200 only): 1) Kernel tiling: adjust QK tile from 128x128 -> 128x64 for the fp8_qk_gemm path when (head_dim=128, q_len <= 64) to reduce smem and register pressure; keep existing path for long-context prefill. 2) Launch config: update CTA mapping (warps per CTA) from 8 -> 6 for selected shapes to increase active CTAs/SM; clamp dynamic smem to stay under 96KB by default and enable 128KB smem opt-in when the device reports it and occupancy remains >= 2 CTAs/SM. 3) Pipelining: for Hopper, enable a deeper cp.async stage count for K/V load when sequence length is small to hide latency; keep previous stage count for larger tiles to avoid register spill. 4) Heuristics table: add a Hopper tuning table keyed by (phase=prefill|decode, head_dim, q_len bucket, kv_len bucket, gqa_factor) and emit the chosen config into the perf trace span when kernel tracing is enabled. 5) Microbench: add a focused fp8_attention_microbench that runs a matrix of representative shapes (decode-heavy + prefill-heavy) and reports kernel time + achieved TFLOPs; emits JSON to match benchmark-lab ingestion.

Microbench results (perf-lab, CUDA 12.4, driver 550.54; numbers are median of 50 iters after warmup; absolute values will vary, focus on deltas): - H100 SXM (sm90): decode (B=16, q_len=1, kv_len=4096, head_dim=128, gqa=8): kernel time -9.8% (from 41.2us -> 37.2us), achieved TFLOPs +10.6%. - H100 SXM: prefill (B=8, q_len=1024, kv_len=1024, head_dim=128, gqa=8): kernel time -3.1%. - H200 SXM (sm90): decode (B=32, q_len=1, kv_len=8192, head_dim=128, gqa=8): kernel time -11.4%. - H200 SXM: prefill (B=4, q_len=2048, kv_len=2048, head_dim=128, gqa=8): kernel time -2.7%.

Correctness: No math changes to accumulation or scaling; this is tiling/launch/pipe changes only. Added a deterministic comparison test vs the previous kernel config for a small set of shapes with fixed RNG seed (max abs diff and relative error thresholds consistent with existing FP8 tolerances).

Testing: - unit: //runtime/kernels:fp8_attention_tests (pass) - microbench: //runtime/kernels:fp8_attention_microbench (pass; results uploaded to gs://perf-lab/redwood/pr-10622/ ) - integration: ran redwood-infer smoke on H100 (single-node) with FP8 enabled (pass)

Rollout notes: Changes are gated on device capability (sm90) and the new heuristics table; other GPUs unchanged. If we see unexpected regressions in end-to-end TTFT/TPOT, we can disable via runtime config `RUNTIME_FP8_ATTN_HOPPER_TUNING=0` (added in this PR). This PR is intended to be paired with benchmark harness work in ENG-24810; follow-up will wire the microbench JSON into the broader report generator.

Docs: Added short notes in runtime/perf/README.md on how to run the microbench and interpret the output.

Risk / mitigations: Main risk is shape mis-bucketing leading to worse performance for some long-context prefill. Mitigated by (a) leaving the existing long-context tile path unchanged, (b) conservative smem clamp to keep occupancy reasonable, (c) tracing of chosen config when perf tracing is enabled for fast attribution.

Checklist: [x] Perf numbers attached (H100 + H200) [x] Added/updated tests [x] No behavior change for non-Hopper [x] Added rollback knob
commits: kernels(fp8-attn): add Hopper tuning table + capability gating
kernels(fp8-attn): adjust QK tile/warps for common decode shapes
kernels(fp8-attn): cp.async stage tuning + smem clamp
tests: add fp8 attention microbench + JSON emitter
review_conversation:
Hiro Tanaka: The delta on decode looks great. Can you confirm we don’t accidentally pick the 128KB smem path on nodes configured for 96KB max? Also would like to see occupancy numbers for the tuned configs.

Grace Kim (author): Good call. Added an explicit clamp to 96KB unless the device reports 128KB and we can maintain >=2 CTAs/SM. Also added a microbench print of achieved occupancy (via launch bounds + profiler counters) into the JSON output.

Isabella Rossi: For the microbench, can we ensure warmup is long enough to avoid first-iter clock ramp effects? And can we pin GPU clocks in the run instructions?

Grace Kim: Updated microbench to do 200 warmup iters and 50 measured iters by default; documented recommended `nvidia-smi -lgc` settings in runtime/perf/README.md. (Clock pinning is optional but strongly recommended for lab runs.)

Noah Patel: Please double-check that the heuristic buckets include gqa_factor and head_dim explicitly; we’ve had collisions before where head_dim=64 and 128 pick the same config.

Grace Kim: Fixed; the key now includes head_dim and gqa_factor and we have an assertion that the selected config matches the expected head_dim at runtime (debug only).

Yuki Sato: Can we emit the selected tile/warp config to tracing spans behind the existing kernel-trace flag? It’ll help us correlate end-to-end regressions.

Grace Kim: Added `fp8_attn_cfg` fields (tile_mn, warps, stages, smem_bytes) to the kernel-selection span when `RUNTIME_KERNEL_TRACE=1`.

Hiro Tanaka: LGTM after the smem clamp change.

Isabella Rossi: LGTM.

Noah Patel: Approved.
release_notes: Performance: Improved FP8 attention kernel performance on H100/H200 for common decode-heavy shapes (single-token decode) via Hopper-specific tiling/launch tuning.
Tooling: Added fp8 attention microbenchmark runner producing JSON artifacts for benchmark ingestion.
Config: Added rollback knob `RUNTIME_FP8_ATTN_HOPPER_TUNING` (default on for sm90).
